item.title: [AINews] Agents for Everything Else: Codex for Knowledge Work, Claude for Creative Work
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Security, a code review tool, amid increasing focus on security vulnerabilities. The article also references Claude Cowork's planning UI as a benchmark comparison point for Codex's new interface design, with Codex explicitly rejecting a Cowork-like toggle in favor of agent-routed UI. Claude Security is a new dedicated code review product worth evaluating for professional security workflows, and the Codex/Cowork UI comparison provides useful context on how Cowork's interaction model is influencing competitor design decisions.

item.title: [AINews] Silicon Valley gets Serious about Services
item.description: Anthropic has formed an unnamed joint venture with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs, funded with $1.5B, to provide enterprise deployment services for Claude. The model involves small teams working alongside Anthropic Applied AI staff to build custom Claude-powered systems tailored to specific organizational operations. This signals Anthropic is moving into direct enterprise implementation services, creating a new channel for professional Claude deployments that could affect how large organizations procure and integrate Claude beyond the standard API.

item.title: [AINews] Anthropic-SpaceXai's 300MW/$5B/yr deal for Colossus I, ARR growth is 8000% annualized
item.description: Anthropic held its second annual developer event announcing a partnership with SpaceX/xAI to take over the Colossus I cluster (estimated ~$5B/year deal), plus three new features for Claude Managed Agents. Dario Amodei highlighted 80x ARR growth and reiterated his 2026 prediction for one-person billion-dollar companies enabled by AI coding agents. The Colossus infrastructure deal signals a major expansion in Claude's compute capacity, and the three new Managed Agents features are directly relevant to practitioners building agentic workflows on Claude.

item.title: [AINews] Codex Rises, Claude Meters Programmatic Usage
item.description: Anthropic has changed its Claude subscription pricing so that each plan now provides a monthly API token credit equal to the dollar value of the subscription (e.g., $200 plan = $200 in API credits), separating 'interactive usage' (claude.ai, Claude Code) from 'programmatic usage' (third-party harnesses). This ends an estimated 70-90% discount that third-party Claude API harnesses previously enjoyed, which users are characterizing as a 'rug pull' despite the policy now being explicit and consistent. Practitioners using Claude through third-party tools or custom API integrations need to account for full API pricing going forward, and should audit their usage costs immediately as the previous informal subsidy is gone.

item.title: Opus 4.6, Codex 5.3, and the post-benchmark era
item.description: Claude Opus 4.6 has been released as a coding assistant, competing directly with OpenAI's GPT-5.3-Codex. The author, who uses Claude Code extensively as a general computer agent for software engineering, data analysis, and automation, finds Opus 4.6 ahead of Codex 5.3 on usability in a broad set of horizontal tasks. Practitioners running Claude Code for agentic workflows beyond pure coding (data analysis, automation, git operations) have a current competitive benchmark against OpenAI's latest coding model, with Opus 4.6 holding an edge in generalist usability.

item.title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
item.description: A member of the Claude Code team at Anthropic argues for using HTML instead of Markdown as a Claude output format, enabling SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, inline annotations, and in-page navigation in responses. The post includes concrete prompt patterns and a curated example gallery demonstrating richer information delivery compared to flat Markdown output. Switching to HTML output requests unlocks Claude's ability to generate self-contained, visually structured artifacts—useful for code review, technical explanations, and ad-hoc analysis where navigability and visual encoding add real value.

item.title: PolicyDec 18, 2025Project Vend: Phase twoIn June, we revealed that we’d set up a small shop in our San Francisco office lunchroom, run by an AI shopkeeper. It was part of Project Vend, a free-form experiment exploring how well AIs could do on complex, real-world tasks. How has Claude's business been since we last wrote?
item.description: Anthropic published a follow-up on Project Vend, an ongoing real-world experiment running a physical shop in their SF office operated autonomously by Claude. The update covers Claude's performance as an AI shopkeeper since the June 2025 initial reveal, testing complex agentic decision-making in a commercial context. Provides concrete data on Claude's real-world agentic capabilities in open-ended commercial tasks, relevant for practitioners designing autonomous Claude-powered workflows.

item.title: Societal ImpactsMar 18, 2026What 81,000 people want from AIWe invited Claude.ai users to share how they use AI, what they dream it could make possible, and what they fear it might do. Nearly 81,000 people participated—the largest and most multilingual qualitative study of its kind. Here's what we found.
item.description: Anthropic conducted a large-scale qualitative study of 81,000 Claude.ai users to understand how they use AI, their aspirations for it, and their fears. The study is described as the largest and most multilingual qualitative research of its kind on AI user perspectives. Understanding the documented use patterns, aspirations, and concerns of tens of thousands of Claude users provides practitioners with data-backed insight into real-world deployment contexts and user expectations.

item.title: ResearchApr 24, 2026Project DealWe created a marketplace for employees in our San Francisco office, with one big twist. We tasked Claude with buying, selling and negotiating on our colleagues’ behalf.
item.description: Anthropic ran an internal experiment called Project Deal, deploying Claude as an autonomous agent to buy, sell, and negotiate in a real marketplace among SF office employees. This tests Claude's agentic capabilities in multi-party negotiation and economic decision-making in a live environment. Provides concrete data on how Claude performs as an autonomous negotiation agent in real-world multi-stakeholder scenarios, directly relevant to practitioners building agentic Claude applications.

item.title: AlignmentMay 8, 2026Teaching Claude whyNew research on how we've reduced agentic misalignment.
item.description: Anthropic published new research on reducing agentic misalignment in Claude, detailing how they've worked on teaching Claude the reasoning behind its guidelines rather than just the rules. A separate study, 'Project Deal,' tested Claude autonomously buying, selling, and negotiating on behalf of Anthropic employees in a real marketplace. The agentic misalignment research directly affects how Claude behaves in autonomous/agentic workflows, and the negotiation experiment provides concrete data on Claude's real-world performance in multi-step, goal-directed tasks.

item.title: Natural Language Autoencoders: Turning Claude’s thoughts into textInterpretabilityMay 7, 2026AI models like Claude talk in words but think in numbers. In this study we train Claude to translate its thoughts into human-readable text.
item.description: Anthropic published research on Natural Language Autoencoders, a technique that trains Claude to translate its internal numeric representations (activations) into human-readable text. This interpretability work bridges the gap between Claude's internal 'thinking' in vector space and understandable language. For practitioners working on Claude reliability, alignment, or debugging, this research offers a new mechanism for inspecting what Claude is internally representing during inference, which could inform prompt engineering and trust assessment.

item.title: What is the Enterprise plan?
item.description: Anthropic's Enterprise plan is now available for self-serve purchase directly on their website, removing the previous requirement to go through a Sales team. The new self-serve Enterprise tier includes a unified seat type covering Claude, Claude Code, and Cowork. Organizations can now immediately provision Enterprise-level access to all Claude tools without sales cycle delays, streamlining procurement for professional teams.

item.title: Access usage data with the Analytics API
item.description: Anthropic has released an Enterprise Analytics API that provides programmatic access to daily usage and engagement data for Claude and Claude Code Remote within an organization. Data is aggregated per organization per day, with each endpoint returning a snapshot for a specified date. Enterprise teams can now automate usage reporting and integrate Claude/Claude Code consumption metrics into their own dashboards or cost-management systems instead of relying on manual console checks.

item.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 4.6

The model includes a 1M token context window available in beta. Practitioners using Sonnet for agentic workflows, coding tasks, or long-document processing should evaluate the upgraded capabilities and the 1M token context window for applicable use cases.

item.title: Manage Cowork plugins for your organization

item.title: Schedule recurring tasks in Cowork

Task scheduling in Cowork enables automation workflows that run without manual triggers, expanding what's possible for professional desktop automation use cases.

item.title: Import and export your memory from Claude
item.description: Anthropic has added import and export functionality for Claude's memory system, allowing users to transfer their stored memories in and out of Claude. This feature gives users direct control over the data Claude retains about them across conversations. Professionals can now back up, audit, migrate, or bulk-edit Claude's persistent memory rather than being locked into whatever Claude has accumulated over time.

item.title: Use Claude’s chat search and memory to build on previous context

Professionals using Claude can now leverage persistent memory and searchable chat history to maintain continuity across sessions, reducing the need to re-establish context repeatedly.

item.title: Custom visuals in chat

item.title: Assign tasks to Claude from anywhere in Cowork
item.description: Anthropic is rolling out a persistent agent thread feature in Cowork, allowing Pro and Max plan users to assign tasks to Claude from Claude Desktop or Claude for iOS/Android. Max plans get access starting today, with Pro plans following over the next two days. Pro and Max subscribers can now manage Cowork automation tasks remotely via mobile or desktop without being at their primary machine.

item.title: Put Claude to work on your computer
item.description: Anthropic has launched computer use capability within Cowork (formerly Dispatch) for Pro and Max plan users, allowing Claude to directly operate files, dev tools, and UI elements on a user's machine with no setup required. The feature enables autonomous task execution on the user's computer while they are away. Pro and Max plan subscribers can now delegate multi-step computer tasks to Claude in Cowork, potentially automating workflows that previously required manual interaction or custom scripting.

item.title: Let Claude use your computer in Cowork
item.description: Anthropic has added computer use capability to Cowork (formerly Dispatch) for Pro and Max plan users, enabling Claude to directly control the computer—opening files, running dev tools, clicking, and navigating the screen autonomously. No setup is required, and the feature activates while the user is away. Pro and Max subscribers can now delegate multi-step computer tasks to Claude without writing automation scripts or configuring external tools, significantly expanding what can be handed off to agentic workflows.

item.title: Use interactive connectors in Claude
item.description: Claude's mobile app now supports interactive connectors that render live charts, diagrams, and shareable assets visually within conversations. This extends beyond static responses to fully interactive app integrations. Practitioners can now build and share dynamic visual artifacts directly in Claude mobile conversations, expanding use cases for data visualization and collaborative workflows on mobile.

item.title: managing custom roles
item.description: Anthropic has added role-based access control to Claude's admin tools, allowing admins to organize users into groups (manually or via SCIM) and assign custom roles that define which Claude capabilities each group can access. This includes the ability to enable Claude Cowork selectively for specific teams and restrict features by department. Enterprise Claude deployments can now implement granular capability gating and spend controls per team, enabling staged rollouts of features like Cowork without org-wide exposure.

item.title: managing group spend limit
item.description: Anthropic has added group-based permission management to Claude's admin console, allowing admins to organize users into groups (manually or via SCIM) and assign custom roles controlling which Claude capabilities each group can access. Admins can now enable Claude Cowork for specific teams, restrict features by department, and set per-group spend limits. Enterprise admins can now implement granular, role-based access control for Claude tools including Cowork, enabling staged rollouts and departmental governance without blanket restrictions.

item.title: setting up role-based permissions
item.description: Anthropic has added role-based permissions to Claude's admin console, allowing admins to organize users into groups (manually or via SCIM) and assign custom roles controlling access to specific Claude capabilities. Enterprise Claude deployments can now implement granular access control and staged rollouts of features like Cowork without giving all users the same capability set.

item.title: Monitor Claude Cowork activity with OpenTelemetry
item.description: Anthropic has added OpenTelemetry support to Claude Cowork, enabling monitoring and observability of desktop automation activity. The feature allows practitioners to instrument and trace Cowork sessions using the OpenTelemetry standard. Teams running Cowork in production workflows can now integrate activity monitoring into existing observability stacks for debugging, auditing, and performance analysis.

item.title: View usage analytics for Team and Enterprise plans

item.title: Claude Enterprise Analytics API: Access engagement and adoption data

Enterprise teams deploying Cowork can now integrate adoption and engagement data into their existing analytics pipelines and dashboards to track usage at scale.
